compare-fractions.title: Bridges over the river
compare-fractions.conclusion: The more parts, the smaller each part. And sometimes two fractions are exactly the same size!

halfOrQuarter.narration: Two bridges cross the river. Which one has more wood?
halfOrQuarter.correct: Exactly! One half is more than one quarter.
halfOrQuarter.notYet: Hmm, look closely: which bridge reaches further across the water?
halfOrQuarter.hint: I'll draw lines where the wood ends. Which line is further across?

sameParts.narration: Both bridges have five planks of the same size. Where are more laid?
sameParts.correct: Right! Four fifths are more than two fifths.
sameParts.notYet: Almost! Count the planks that are already laid.
sameParts.hint: Look at the lines: where does the wood reach further?

buildThreeQuarters.narration: Now you build! The bridge has four planks. Lay three quarters of it.
buildThreeQuarters.correct: Great building! Three of four planks are three quarters.
buildThreeQuarters.notYet: The bridge still wobbles. Three quarters means three of four planks.
buildThreeQuarters.hint: I'll count with you. Tap the planks until there are three.

moreParts.narration: The upper bridge has three planks, the lower one six. Where is more wood: one third or one sixth?
moreParts.correct: Brilliant! More parts means each part is smaller. One third is more.
moreParts.notYet: Six is more than three, that's true. But look how small the sixth planks are!
moreParts.hint: Look at the lines: where does the wood end?

twoQuartersHalf.narration: And now? Two quarters on top, one half below.
twoQuartersHalf.correct: The same! Two quarters are exactly one half.
twoQuartersHalf.notYet: Hmm, compare where the wood ends.
twoQuartersHalf.hint: The lines help: are they in the same place?

side.title: Write with {name}
side.hintCompare: Write for example: top, bottom or same.
side.hintBuild: Write how many planks you lay, for example: 2.

compare-bridges.narration: Look at the two bridges. Which one has more wood?
compare-bridges.correct: Exactly! You can compare the fractions in your task the same way.
compare-bridges.notYet: Hmm, look again: which bridge reaches further across the water?
compare-bridges.hint: I'll draw lines where the wood ends. Which one is further across?

build-bridge.correct: Great building! That is what this fraction looks like.
build-bridge.notYet: The bridge still wobbles. Count the planks again.
build-bridge.hint: I'll count with you. Tap the planks.

number-line.narration: We start at {start} and jump {steps} {sign, select, minus {back} other {forward}}. Where do we land?
number-line.correct: Exactly, at {landing}! You can jump the same way in your task.
number-line.notYet: Almost! Count the steps again from {start}.
number-line.hint: I'll show you every step. Count along!

groups-total.narration: Here are {groups} plates with {each} dots each. How many dots are there in all?
groups-total.correct: Right, {total}! {groups} times {each} is {total}. Try your task the same way.
groups-total.hint: I'll number the dots. Count along!

groups-each.narration: {total} dots are shared fairly onto {groups} plates. How many does each plate get?
groups-each.correct: Exactly, {each} on each plate! You can share the same way in your task.
groups-each.notYet: Almost! Share the dots out one by one.
groups-each.hint: I'll share them out for you, one by one.
